claims.text: The starting material is a polycrystalline equiatomic Hf-Nb-Ti-V-Zr solid solution containing 20 at.% of each element.
Equiatomic HfNbTiVZr has an average valence electron concentration of approximately 4.40.
Equiatomic HfNbTiVZr has a superconducting critical temperature of approximately 0.5 K.
Replacing 5 at.% Zr with Nb produces Hf20Nb25Ti20V20Zr15.
The Nb-for-Zr substitution raises the calculated average VEC from approximately 4.40 to 4.45.
Average valence electron concentration is the primary governor of superconducting Tc in the specified Hf-Nb-Ti-V-Zr alloys.
Increasing VEC raises the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
A higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level enhances the electron-phonon coupling constant.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling raises the superconducting critical temperature.
The Nb-enriched alloy will have a Tc approximately 0.1-0.3 K above the 0.5 K baseline.
The Nb-enriched alloy will exhibit a larger heat-capacity jump at Tc than the baseline alloy.

The proposed VEC-Tc relationship applies to single-phase five-element solid solutions whose constituent concentrations remain within 5 at.% of equiatomic and whose average VEC is approximately 4.0-4.8.
The proposed relationship is not expected to hold if partial ordering or secondary phases form.
The proposed relationship is not expected to hold when VEC exceeds approximately 5.0.
Changes in phonon spectra and disorder scattering can affect the magnitude of the Tc shift.
A Tc change of zero or less within a ±0.05 K comparison uncertainty would falsify the proposed positive Tc response.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis calls the investigated alloys equimolar, but the proposed modified alloy is Hf20Nb25Ti20V20Zr15 and therefore is not strictly equimolar. The boundary's phrase 'equimolar (±5 at.%)' partially accommodates this composition but uses equimolar inconsistently.
